assessment: The optokinetic reflex (OKR) is a behavioral response that moves the eye so as to keep the image on the retina stabilized during the animal's movements. This important study traces the origins of that behavior down to cellular mechanisms of circuits in the retina. Specifically, it offers compelling evidence that the asymmetries and tuning properties of the OKR are shaped by the excitation/inhibition balance in retinal circuits and the regulation of spiking thresholds across different neuron types.
